title: Dungeon Run (2011) - Introduction
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0irTZK6Z_YI

Daniel (@dungeondive) opens a short series on Dungeon Run, the 2011 competitive dungeon crawl Plaid Hat Games set in its Summoner Wars universe and then, by his account, abandoned. He has heard from people connected to the company that a sequel or full expansion was finished and will almost certainly never ship, and he makes an open appeal for it to appear even as a print-and-play.

The design he describes is unusual. Up to six heroes explore random tiles, fighting monsters and looting encounters, cooperating or sabotaging one another as they like, until someone finds the boss room. Whoever kills the boss claims the Summoning Stone and becomes the boss themselves. From that moment every other player is hunting them, and the game turns into tag: win by walking out of the dungeon with the stone. Daniel can think of few comparisons beyond Dungeoneer and Masmorra, and he sold Masmorra after two plays.

The official solo rules strip out the special character cards for a points-attack mode he dislikes, so his series will run a two-player game with one hand tied. Aldegar Vain, a paladin, is the hero he is rooting for; Stabbins the goblin will act on a die roll, helping on odds and hindering on evens. He walks through the setup, praises how little there is to teach compared to the genre's usual fiddliness, and confesses that his completionist streak is costing him too much money.

----

Dungeon Run turns the endgame into a game of tag the moment someone kills the boss. Does a competitive crawl need a twist like that to work, or is one-versus-many the genre's natural shape?
